clue.text: Schemer has design said to come to nothing

indicators.note: to come to means the next piece is added on at the end
said tells us the letters are what a speaker would pronounce, not what is spelt

parts.note: a design or pattern is a figure, which in a non-rhotic accent can be pronounced with a final 'uh' sound
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A plotter announces that his grand plan is doomed to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure', said aloud, gives FIGAR, which then has O (nothing) added after it; 'to come to nothing' reads like failure but is the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro, the barber of Beaumarchais's plays and the operas of Rossini and Mozart, is a resourceful intriguer.

clue.text: Overcome by aggressive action — thus king and queen may be invisible

definitions.meaning: to confront and beat an opponent by intimidation

definitions.text: thus king and queen may be invisible
definitions.meaning: playing cards placed this way hide their faces

explanation.surface: Defeating someone by force, while the court cards lie hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The king and queen are playing cards, not royalty: placed with their faces to the table, they cannot be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to defeat by confrontation and also describes cards lying with faces hidden.

clue.text: Place where lawyers are heard to define a wrong in other than black-and-white terms?

indicators.note: heard means the letters come from what is spoken, not spelt

parts.words: a wrong in other than black-and-white terms
parts.note: a grey sin is a wrong that is neither clearly black nor white

explanation.surface: A legal venue where lawyers debate morally ambiguous wrongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To define' links the parts. The spoken 'grey sin' becomes the name of one of the London Inns of Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's Inn is one of the four Inns of Court in London to which barristers belong.

clue.text: Toe of slipper — one little dog gets shred

indicators.note: the toe is the end of a slipper, so its last letter is picked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A puppy chews a slipper to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred something is to tear it into pieces, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: What they did to choose Matthias — a saint among idiots?

definitions.text: What they did to choose Matthias

indicators.note: among means the next pieces are placed within the word for idiots

parts.note: clots are idiots

explanation.surface: A question about how the apostles chose Matthias, oddly hinting at a holy man among fools.
explanation.walkthrough: In Acts 1:26 the apostles chose Matthias to replace Judas by drawing lots.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible says the disciples drew lots to pick between two candidates, so the phrase describes their action.

clue.text: Detective and policeman struggling with brat

indicators.note: struggling means the letters writhe into a different order

explanation.surface: A detective and a policeman wrestle with an unruly youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' links the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Campion is the gentleman sleuth of Margery Allingham's crime novels.

clue.text: Set meals

parts.note: meals eaten in front of the television set, not fixed-price menus

explanation.surface: A restaurant's fixed menu.
explanation.definitionFit: These are ready-made meals designed to be eaten while watching television.

clue.text: Days of celebrating in wide street at end of month

indicators.note: at end of means the street word comes after the month word

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a broad street

explanation.surface: A festival held on a broad street at the end of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In the church calendar an octave is the eight-day period of celebration following a major feast.

clue.text: In a painful way, only changing sides about half way through

indicators.text: changing sides about half way through
indicators.note: changing sides means left becomes right at a point near the middle of the word

parts.note: solely means only

explanation.surface: It hurt, with only the change of ends at half time.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) in SOLELY becomes R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Sorely means grievously or painfully.

clue.text: With a muscular problem an athlete has little power

parts.note: Steve Cram was a famous British middle-distance runner
P is the abbreviation for power, little meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: A sprinter with a pulled muscle finds his strength sapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a' is a link. Steve Cram was a world-champion British miler in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a sudden painful contraction of a muscle.

clue.text: Journalist has bottom pinched by would-be lover

indicators.note: pinched by means held tightly inside the word for a would-be lover

parts.note: a suitor courts someone he hopes to win
a bed is the bottom of a river or sea

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer gets his backside nipped by an amorous admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' tempts the solver towards BUM or REAR; it is BED, as in a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor is a journalist who checks and edits copy before printing.

clue.text: Workers ultimately cry and chairman, MD et al get everything that's going

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of workers

parts.note: weep means cry
the chairman, managing director and others form a company's board of directors

explanation.surface: Staff weep while the directors take every reward on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To win everything available, from a card-game idiom for taking all the stakes.

clue.text: Go spare — paid badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is furious because they were poorly paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go spare' reads as British slang for becoming furious; only 'Go' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To go can mean to vanish or cease to be visible, the same sense as vanish.

clue.text: Volume in Christmas wrapping could be a bestseller

indicators.note: in, paired with wrapping, says the volume letter sits within the Christmas word
wrapping means the Christmas word goes round the volume letter

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: A book given as a Christmas present might sell well.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestseller is often a work of fiction, a long prose story.

clue.text: Employee testing seafood quality possibly not an Oxford type

definitions.meaning: a worker who picks out small sea snails, read literally
a pointed-toed shoe, not a sturdy laced Oxford shoe

explanation.surface: A seafood inspector who, perhaps, never went to Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford here is a type of laced shoe, not the university; the answer is a sharply pointed shoe of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a person who extracts winkles; also the name for a shoe with a long pointed toe, unlike an Oxford.

clue.text: Situationally the uvula must be very deceptive

definitions.meaning: describing where the fleshy flap at the back of the mouth is located
an idiom for telling outrageous falsehoods

explanation.surface: A remark about the uvula leading to a warning about deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must' links the two definitions; the first reads 'lie' as be situated, the second as tell untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in one's throat is an old idiom for lying grossly; literally the uvula is located there.

clue.text: Let's now leave issue that's upsetting country

indicators.note: upsetting means the word for issue is knocked into a different order

parts.note: an item is an issue or matter for discussion
Togo is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Time to leave because a troubling matter is upsetting the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: ITEM rearranged by 'upsetting' gives TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is time to go is an everyday way of suggesting departure.

clue.text: Conscious of emotion when maiden's jilted

indicators.note: jilted means abandoned, so the maiden letter is dropped

parts.note: sentiment means feeling or emotion
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden, an over with no runs

explanation.surface: Aware of a feeling when a young woman has been dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' links definition and wordplay. Remove M from SENTIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive and feel, so aware.

clue.text: State what this, in short, might be? Shan't!

definitions.text: State what this, in short, might be? Shan't!

parts.words: State what this, in short, might be? Shan't!
parts.note: Shan't is a fresh arrangement of Hants, the short form of an English county, giving a US state's name

explanation.surface: A demand to explain something, met with a childish refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the standard abbreviation for the English county; rearranging it gives SHANT, a 'new' version of that county's short name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the original thirteen states of the USA, in New England.

clue.text: High-protein food — what office worker needed first

indicators.note: needed first means the office worker word comes before the what word

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
eh is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: Asking what high-protein snack an office temp needs to start the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempeh is an Indonesian food made from fermented soya beans, rich in protein.

clue.text: Loveless god wanting everybody to be a slave

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, here taken away

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A god without love wishes for everyone to be enslaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrall is a slave or bondsman, a historic synonym.

clue.text: Name of man participating in the thanksgiving?

indicators.note: participating in means the letters are taking part in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking which man is joining the Thanksgiving celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethan is a common male first name.

clue.text: Most illustrious footballer of yesteryear — outside right

indicators.note: outside means the footballer's name goes round the next word

parts.note: George Best was a star of Manchester United in the 1960s
taken as written

explanation.surface: A great former footballer who played on the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside right' looks like a football position, but outside is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The most illustrious is the most brilliant, a figurative use of the superlative.

clue.text: Brood in straw etc beginning to fly off

indicators.note: the beginning letter flies off, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: thatch is straw and similar material used for roofing

explanation.surface: A bird's young in a straw nest, ready to fly off.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood eggs is to sit on them until they hatch, so the two verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: Get cross sewing, issuing simple expression of annoyance

parts.note: plain means simple
darn is a mild oath

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over their needlework and mutters a mild curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issuing' links definition and wordplay. Plain-darning is darning with crossed threads in a simple weave.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a verb for mending fabric with a simple crisscross weave of thread.

clue.text: Rhetorical device in formal statement not right on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means the remaining letters are seen as in a mirror, backwards
not means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a report is a formal account

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a figure of speech in an official statement seems wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from REPORT leaves EPORT, which 'on reflection' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, such as metaphor, used for rhetorical effect.

clue.text: Troubles in old area of land — countryside's not flat here

indicators.note: in means the troubles word sits inside the land measure

parts.note: a hide was an old English measure of farmland
ills are troubles

explanation.surface: Unrest in an ancient piece of territory where the landscape rises.
explanation.walkthrough: A hide was a medieval English measure of land, enough to support a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope is where the countryside is not level, the side of a rise in the land.

clue.text: See 14
